newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil prices seen easing as imports rise.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil prices seen easing as imports rise.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil prices are likely to fall in domestic markets next week amid rising imports, dealers said on Saturday.
Indicative prices of RBD palm oil fell to $575 per tonne C&F Karachi on Saturday from $585 a week earlier due to a surge in imports, a dealer at Saulat Enterprises said.
He said six ships loaded with 78,500 tonnes of palm oil and soyoil would dock in Karachi in the next few days.
Those with palm oil cargoes were the Wawasan Megah with 26,000 tonnes, the Wawasan Courage with 25,000 tonnes, the Bow Princess with 6,000 tonnes and the Sino Kim with 5,500 tonnes.
Vegoil stocks at cooking oil processing mills and warehouses stood at an estimated 129,000 tonnes on Saturday, compared to 118,000 a week earlier, the dealer said.
The state-owned Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) invited bids for 6,000 tonnes of palm oil on Tuesday, but scrapped the auction after getting bids it considered below market prices.
"It is likely to re-invite tenders soon," one dealer said.
Vegoil imports fell 5.39 percent to 56,477 tonnes worth $32 million in January from 59,696 tonnes worth $32 million in December.
